paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: This figure compares the error rate (one average minus test accuracy), computation cost, and GPU memory across our approach and baselines, for fine-tuning Llama-3-8B on ten NLP tasks with QAdapter.

model_annotations.German: The bar chart titled "QAdapter" compares the computational cost, measured in the number of FLOPs (floating-point operations), across several fine-tuning methods for the Llama-3-8B model on ten NLP tasks. The vertical axis, labeled "# FLOPs", is on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10¹⁸ to 10²⁰, with tick marks at 10¹⁸, 10¹⁹, and 10²⁰. The horizontal axis lists six different fine-tuning approaches: "Full FT", "TAG", "Adapter", "MTL-FT", "QAdapter", and "Ours", arranged from left to right in descending order of computational cost. All bars except the last are orange, while the bar for "Ours" is green, visually distinguishing it from the others. The "Full FT" method has the highest FLOPs, reaching approximately 10²⁰. "TAG", "Adapter", and "MTL-FT" have similar costs, each around 10¹⁹. "QAdapter" shows a lower cost, approximately 10¹⁸.5, and "Ours" has the lowest computational cost, slightly below 10¹⁸. The bars are sorted in descending order of FLOPs, and no additional annotations or error bars are present. The chart visually emphasizes the efficiency of the proposed "Ours" method compared to existing baselines.
